City Council Meeting
Public Comment from the Audience
•
If you wish to address the City Council, please complete a Speaker Request Card, as it must be handed to the City Clerk before the start of the meeting.
•
The City Council will hear public comments on matters not listed on the agenda during the Public Comments from the Audience period.
•
Opportunity to address the City Council (on non-agenda items) is limited to 3 minutes per speaker.
•
The City Council will hear public comments on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote.
Brown Act
Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.
Rules of Decorum
Persons attending the meeting shall observe rules of propriety, decorum, good conduct, and refrain from impertinent or slanderous remarks. Violation of this rule shall result in such persons being barred from further audience before the governing body. Pursuant to Gov. Code Sect. 54954.3(c), any person who engages in unlawful interference shall be removed from chambers.
Americans with Disabilities Act
In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please contact the City Clerk's office at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to allow the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to the meeting or service.
This agenda was posted 72 hours in advance of the meeting at the City Hall, 8838 E. Valley Boulevard, Rosemead; the L.A. County Library, Rosemead Branch, 8800 E. Valley Boulevard, Rosemead; and other locations pursuant to RMC Sec. 1.08.020. Any writings or documents provided to a majority of the Rosemead City Council regarding any item on this agenda will be made available for public inspection in the City Clerk's office during normal business hours.

INSTALLATION OF RED CURB AT 9241 VALLEY BOULEVARD
On January 7, 2016, the Traffic Commission reviewed a request for red curb from the property owner of the Orchid Plaza, located at 9241 Valley Boulevard. Specifically, the request is for red curb installation on Valley Boulevard adjacent to the plaza to enhance sight-distance visibility. The City completed a traffic investigation, and found that certain red curb installation adjacent to the driveways will enhance sight distance for vehicles exiting the Plaza.
Recommendation: That the City Council approve the installation of 30 feet of red curb between the two existing driveways to the Orchid Plaza, and 15 feet of red curb immediately to the east of the easterly driveway.
Staff Report
C.
LETTER TO LOS ANGELES COUNTY SUPERVISOR HILDA SOLIS IN SUPPORT OF A COUNTY ORDINANCE FOR PHARMACEUTICALS AND SHARPS COLLECTION AND DISPOSAL
The City Council will consider a request by the Los Angeles County Integrated Waste Management Task Force for a letter of support for a County ordinance regulating pharmaceutical and sharps collection and disposal.
Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the Mayor to sign a letter to Supervisor Hilda Solis in support of adoption of a County ordinance for pharmaceuticals and sharps collection and disposal.
Staff Report

KLINGERMAN STREET/ANGELUS AVENUE INTERSECTION TRAFFIC EVALUATION
On January 26, 2016, after hearing a technical presentation from Willdan Engineering, the City Council directed staff to further review the intersection of Klingerman Street and Angelus Avenue. Specifically, the City was directed to review other agenciesâ€™ (i.e Pico Rivera, Monterey Park) engineering practices for similar situations, and bring back a Resolution for consideration by the City Council.
The City has since contacted the cities of Pico Rivera and Monterey Park. Additionally, the Cityâ€™s Public Works Manager (a licensed engineer) has conducted further review of the intersection, and determined that the installation of all-way â€œSTOPâ€ control at the Klingerman/Angelus intersection would reduce conflicts between vehicles exiting driveways and through traffic, and enhance traffic safety.
Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution 2016-07, approving the installation of All-Way â€œSTOPâ€ control at the Klingerman/Angelus intersection.

MATTERS FROM CITY MANAGER & STAFF
A.
MID-YEAR BUDGET AMENDMENTS
The City Council will consider adjustments to the current Budget for the 2015-16 Fiscal Year. During any fiscal year, unforeseen financial needs and opportunities typically arise which require Council approval of adjustments to projected revenues and expenditures. At this time there are several items that will require appropriations as well as projected revenue adjustments. The net impact of all recommended adjustments to the General Fund operating budget are positive, reflecting more anticipated revenues than expenditures.
Recommendation: That the City Council approve Resolution No. 2016-06 approving various appropriations for the remainder of the current fiscal year.
Staff Report
B.
ZAPOPAN PARK IMPROVEMENT PROJECT â€“ DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION UPDATE
As part of the Fiscal Year 2014-15 (FY 14-15) Budget, the City Council approved the Zapopan Park Improvement Project (Project No. 41008), and allocated $1,050,000 in redevelopment bond funds for the design and construction effort. The City has recently obtained approval from Southern California Edison (SCE) for the improvements, as well as substantially completed the design. A presentation regarding the most recent design and construction schedule will be made at the City Council meeting.
Recommendation: That the City Council provide direction regarding the final project improvements scope and construction bidding strategies.
